“You’re very early, aren’t you?” he observed at last, eyes darting a quick glance over her shoulder as if hoping someone would arrive to break the awkwardness.

But no one else came in, and Mara found herself still holding Jonah’s hand as she watched him scan the room. He shook his head with a casual, conspiratorial expression, as if they were sharing an inside joke about being here together.
“Adrian and Livia will be along shortly,” he said. “They’re finishing up some things. Why don’t you come and have a seat?”
The young man turned toward the couch again, gesturing for her to join him in it. She followed his lead, settling into the cushions beside him while he let go of her hand.
text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

The two pairs of eyes held each other through an entire exhale.
And then the young man had pushed himself up on the armrests, stretched to his full height, and strolled over to shake her hand.
“Mara?”
He was closer than she would have guessed from where he’d been sitting, broad-shouldered and strong-chinned in a white T-shirt, grinning at her through dark-framed glasses as he reached out for the handshake. She took it.
“Jonah,” he said.
“Hello,” she replied, and then they stood there, still shaking hands, not knowing what to do next.

“You’re very early, aren’t you?” he observed at last, eyes darting a quick glance over her shoulder as if hoping someone would arrive to break the awkwardness.

But no one else came in, and Mara found herself still holding Jonah’s hand as she watched him scan the room. He shook his head with a casual, conspiratorial expression, as if they were sharing an inside joke about being here together.
“Adrian and Livia will be along shortly,” he said. “They’re finishing up some things. Why don’t you come and have a seat?”
The young man turned toward the couch again, gesturing for her to join him in it. She followed his lead, settling into the cushions beside him while he let go of her hand.

segment:
The grip was dry and steady, a little firmer than hers but not threatening. She let herself follow his movements as he pulled back toward his original position; the left arm moved with the right, raising until they were both standing straight again. And then the other hand detached from her own and rose as well, to push up his glasses with a finger.
His head was tilted toward her. “I wasn’t expecting you at this hour,” he said in a low voice.
